### Analysis of Divisibility Properties of $a_n$
The sequence was found to have the closed form: $a_n = 6^n + 2^n + 3^n - 1$.
If $k$ is coprime to every $a_n$, then $k$ cannot share any prime factors with any $a_n$. We investigate constraints on $k$ based on divisibility by small primes $p$.

### Part 1: Formal Proof

    $$a_n \equiv 6^n + 2^n + 3^n - 1 \equiv 0^n + (-1)^n + 0^n - 1 \pmod{3}$$
    $$a_n \equiv (-1)^n - 1 \pmod{3}$$

This single finding formally proves that the set of primes that divide every number in $(a_n)$ is a proper subset of the set of all primes.

### Part 2: Determining $k$

For a positive integer $k$ to be relatively prime to every number in $(a_n)$, $k$ must not share any prime factors with any $a_n$. Let $P_{all}$ be the set of all prime factors of any term $a_n$. $k$ must be composed only of primes $p \notin P_{all}$.
